column3: The Hebrew repeats “there” with both Miriam’s death and burial; BSB states the location once.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “when our brothers perished”; BSB expresses this as perishing “with our brothers.”
The Hebrew says “to die there”; BSB says “to die here.”
The Hebrew joins the listed crops with “and”; BSB uses “or” before the last item.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB gives a single “said.”
The Hebrew says the rock will “give” its water; BSB says “pour out.”
The Hebrew actively says “as He commanded him”; BSB uses the passive “as he had been commanded.”
The Hebrew says “he said” without repeating the speaker’s name; BSB explicitly names Moses.
The Hebrew states that the congregation and their livestock drank; BSB describes them as being “able to drink.”
The Hebrew says “before the eyes of the sons of Israel”; BSB uses “in the sight of the Israelites.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “Egypt” and says “many days”; BSB uses “where” for the second occurrence and says “many years.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Edom speaks in the singular, with “me” and “I”; BSB uses plural “our land” and “we.”
The Hebrew shifts from “we” to singular “I,” “my livestock,” and “my feet”; BSB continues with “we” and “our” and says “on foot.”
The Hebrew has an unnamed singular speaker and says Edom went out to meet “him”; BSB names Edom and the Israelites and uses plural “they” for Edom.
The Hebrew refers to Edom with singular pronouns; BSB uses plural “their” and “them.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has both “said” and “saying”; BSB gives a single “said.”
The Hebrew says “My mouth,” rendered “My command” in BSB.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “his garments” without the explicit qualifier “priestly,” and says Aaron will “be gathered” without adding “to his people” in this verse; BSB supplies both.
The Hebrew says “before the eyes of all the congregation”; BSB uses “in the sight of the whole congregation.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names Aaron twice; BSB uses “him” for the second occurrence.
